nodes.statement: Prove the exact normalized consecutive-gap limsup is +∞ for the Ω≤2 sequence.
AFFIRMATIVE CLOSE: prove the canonical proposition exactly as stated, with every quantifier, domain restriction, asymptotic qualifier, and structural condition preserved.
Produce B<∞ and K such that every k≥K satisfies (u_{k+1}−u_k)/log k≤B, or an exactly equivalent negation of limsup=+∞.
NEGATIVE CLOSE: prove that the normalized gaps have finite limsup; equivalently, prove an eventual finite upper bound for (u_{k+1}−u_k)/log k.
Let $1\leq u_1<u_2<\cdots$ be the sequence of integers with at most $2$ prime factors. Is it true that\[\limsup \frac{u_{k+1}-u_k}{\log k}=\infty?\]
Exact-mode audit: all residual-touching comparisons are literal or Fraction-exact; fail-closed behavior verified by deterministic injection tests.
